en.name: Aburaage
en.summary: Aburaage keeps 5–7 days refrigerated and 1–2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). The Japanese manufacturing guidance for 油揚げ specifies chilled storage at 10 °C or below with a use-by of roughly one week; a home fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below sits comfortably inside that.
en.pantry: Not a room-temperature food. Aburaage is thin tofu that has been deep-fried, and although the frying dries the surface, the inside is still a moist, low-acid soy product — exactly the sort of thing that spoils quickly once warm. It must be chilled promptly and kept chilled, and anything left out follows the two-hour rule, one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F). The oil on the surface is a second clock running in parallel: it goes rancid whether or not anything grows.
en.fridge: 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in its pack or a sealed box, and to the printed date if that is sooner. Pour boiling water over the sheets before you cook them — the 油抜き step — which strips the surface oil, improves the flavour and removes what would otherwise be the first thing to go stale. Once a pack is opened, reseal it tightly: aburaage is thin and dries out fast, and it will also take up fridge odours through that porous fried surface.
en.freezer: 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), lying flat in a sealed bag with the air pressed out. Freeze the sheets in the shape you will use them — whole for inari, halved as pockets, or shredded for miso soup and rice — because a frozen sheet is hard to cut neatly. What limits the window is the oil going rancid rather than microbial spoilage, and kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond it; the smell is your guide.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, or drop shredded pieces straight into a simmering pan from frozen. Never thaw on the counter. Sheets thawed in the fridge and still at or below 4 °C (40 °F) may be refrozen with some quality loss.
spoilage: A sour or sharply fermented smell when the pack is opened.
A slimy or sticky surface on the sheets.
A stale, crayon-like smell from the fried surface, which is the oil going rancid.
Any mould spot, in which case the whole pack goes out.
tips: Pour boiling water over the sheets before cooking to remove surface oil.
Freeze them flat and in the shape you will use.
Reseal an opened pack tightly; thin sheets dry out very quickly.
Buy from a chilled cabinet, never a shelf — this is a refrigerated product.

faq.a: 5–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or to the printed date if sooner. Frozen, 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze the sheets flat in the shape you will use them, since a frozen sheet is hard to cut.

faq.q: Why pour boiling water over aburaage?
faq.a: It strips the surface oil, which improves the flavour and removes the part of the sheet that goes stale first.

zh.name: 日式豆皮
zh.summary: 日式豆皮冷藏可放 5～7 天，−18 °C 冷凍是 1～2 個月。日本針對油揚げ的製造指引要求在 10 °C 以下冷藏、有效期約一週；家用冰箱的 4 °C 以下，完全落在這個範圍內。
zh.pantry: 這不是常溫食品。日式豆皮是薄豆腐下鍋油炸的產物，雖然油炸讓表面變乾，裡面仍然是含水量高、低酸的黃豆製品——正是那種一回溫就壞得很快的東西。它必須盡快冷藏、持續冷藏；擺在外面的適用兩小時原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時只有一小時。而且表面的油是同時在跑的第二個時鐘：不管有沒有東西長起來，它都會油耗。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天，連原包裝或裝密封盒；若印製日期更早，以日期為準。下鍋前請用滾水淋過（油抜き），把表面的油沖掉——這會讓味道更好，也去掉了整片豆皮上最先走味的部分。拆封後要確實封好：豆皮很薄，乾得很快，而且那層多孔的炸面很會吸冰箱的味道。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 1～2 個月，平放、壓出空氣密封裝袋。請照你之後要用的形狀冷凍——整片做稻荷壽司、對切成口袋，或切絲給味噌湯和飯用——因為凍硬的豆皮很難切得整齊。限制這段期間的是油脂油耗，不是微生物腐敗；只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全，請以氣味為準。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，或把切絲的直接從冷凍丟進滾著的鍋裡。絕對不要在檯面上解凍。在冷藏解凍、且維持在 4 °C 以下的可以再冷凍，只是品質會打折。
spoilage: 打開包裝聞到酸味或刺鼻的發酵味。
豆皮表面變得黏滑或黏手。
炸面聞起來陳、有蠟筆味，那是油脂油耗了。
只要出現霉點，整包丟掉。
tips: 下鍋前用滾水淋過，把表面的油沖掉。
照之後要用的形狀平放冷凍。
拆封後確實密封；薄薄的豆皮乾得非常快。
要在冷藏櫃買，不要買常溫架上的——這是冷藏產品。

faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 5～7 天，或以更早的印製日期為準。冷凍則是 −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～2 個月。照要用的形狀平放冷凍，因為凍硬之後很難切。

faq.q: 為什麼要用滾水淋豆皮？
faq.a: 那會沖掉表面的油，讓味道更好，也去掉整片豆皮上最先走味的部分。
